description: stat-09: Wilson 95% score intervals (z = 1.96) for per-sub-attack recalls (Fig. 4, Fig. 9, tree runs) and the Dst/Src seen shares of Table 13
fig4_note: The pilot (split_pilot/subattack_results.json, median imputation) stored n_test and a 4-decimal recall but no predictions: k = round(recall n); k_min/k_max bound the rounding and conservative_lo/hi span their Wilson limits. The tree_protocol XGBoost raw s42 runs (NaN -> 0 imputation, a different pipeline) are added with exact counts (in_fig4 = false).
table13_note: n = n_test_period of the drift JSON (the share is taken over test-period FLOWS, temporal_drift_analysis.py), share rounded to 3 decimals: count exact for n <= 1000. Flows to the same destination are not independent, so the Wilson interval (i.i.d. flows) is a lower bound on the uncertainty, most of all when few distinct destinations carry the test period.
iid_note: All Wilson intervals treat the test flows of a group as independent Bernoulli trials (conditional on the fitted model); flows of one session or episode are correlated, so the intervals are optimistic for large, bursty captures (see revision_analyses.py part c for a block bootstrap).
fig9_note: deep_split stored no predictions: n per sub-attack from the tree run with the same test rows (same splits() call), k = round(recall n). Cells (per model, and 'Deep mean (ResNet1D/GRU/Transformer)' = the pooled mean shown in Fig. 9): mean, SD, min-max over runs; ci_mean_lo/hi = mean of the per-run Wilson limits (the interval of the run mean when the runs err on the same flows: conservative); envelope = widest per-run limits. runs: 'all', 'paper runs' (deep_split only), 'epochs_run>=...' (the filter of Fig. 9) and 'paper runs, epochs_run>=...' (= Fig. 9 as published); a subset with the same runs as an earlier one is not repeated.
